name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle020
definition_title: Stored zeta stages, local cover indices, and original-input catalogs
natural_language_statement:
For a width-$L$ subset function $f$, a cutoff, and a compact-table base, the zeta-stage program computes the compact stride and applies one coordinate pass per bit, retaining stages $0,\ldots,L$. Its invariant records every completed stage and preservation outside the stage array. The local-cover matrix entry is a Boolean support indicator obtained from left/right mask hashes, their actual histograms, and bucket-cap flags. Its row candidates are the ordered radix enumeration of weights; its columns decode an ordered pair of residues modulo the selected local prime. Greedy choice indices and occurrence-to-candidate lookup preserve that ordering, including repeated choices.

For an original list of signed integers and modulus $P$, the guarded A-key interface retains all physical positions in each of the three lifts. A wanted incidence satisfies divisibility of its lifted residue plus the common offset minus the global output key. Three parallel catalog arrays store a value, its owner slot, and its sorted position. Programs construct flagged owner records, append only a flagged record's truncated A band, and compute its exact weighted modular score, returning zero for an unflagged record. A separate four-procedure original-input fallback scans triples with three distinct indices for the finite exceptional size regime.

The finite ledger defines six reporting counts: table construction, source encoding, prefix boxes, initial queries, active-prefix queries, and terminal work. For a natural-valued function $f$ and real exponent $a$, its power-bound interface means

$$\forall\varepsilon>0,\quad f(n)\le n^{a+\varepsilon}\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n.$$

These finite counts remain separate from actual machine execution costs. Further programs normalize three supplied color classes, construct their bands and owner tables, decode a physical global-output index into forward-ordered occurrence and mask rows, construct every original A-key lift, and compute independent endpoint flags from a global mask.

The bundle supplies the exact array meanings and finite work quantities used to connect the combinatorial runtime ledger to the deterministic integer 3SUM machine. It preserves original-position multiplicities and avoids replacing physical record identity by equality of key values.

name: ThreeSum1960614_Machine_Bundle021
definition_title: Original-source stages, owner catalogs, and sparse-box lookups
natural_language_statement:
The source-stage program constructs a trimmed source table from a physical signed input array and then builds all compact suffix-zeta stages. Its procedure records identify literal bodies and their callees, rather than postulating execution behavior. A stage lookup constructs its own compact size and subset address and reads one stage cell. For valid masks $U\subseteq Q$, a sparse-box query computes the difference mask $Q\setminus U$, chooses the appropriate prefix stage from the least coordinate of $U$ (or the final stage when $U$ is empty), and reads the corresponding stored signed box value.

A residue join iterates over each left original-position code and visits precisely the matching retained right bucket, emitting every matching position pair once. The uniform stage interface defines executable integer wanted- and false-mass budgets by division of the concrete size majorants by the radix. The arithmetic budget uses maximum modulus $R(n)(4V(n))^2$, where $R$ is the chosen radix and $V$ the prime-window parameter; its per-triple budget is an explicit constant times the rounded modular-counting power, band size times bit budget, and one.

The owner-catalog program writes the three rectangular record families in BC, AB, AC order, preserving each record's permanent physical slot. The flattened A catalog packs values, owner slots and sorted positions, appending only flagged records' truncated bands. Aggregate scoring scans those physical records and sums their exact weighted modular scores. The color-band constructor starts from the original input, computes index colors and class headers, then normalizes and partitions each class using buffers bounded by the original input length.

Constructed local-cover tables are specified by their mask hashes, bucket histograms, support matrix and occurrence-indexed coefficient rows. The global-output decoder interface identifies its two rows with the original record's occurrence indices and subset masks, even when distinct records have equal keys. Concrete trimming-count interfaces use the selected occurrence-to-candidate index list.

These definitions connect original input data, exact stored transforms, and permanent owner/output identities throughout the complete deterministic integer 3SUM proof. The size-only budgets are explicit finite arithmetic objects, not substitutes for the separate machine execution theorems.
